correctness.rationale: Each character weights the edge subset by the product of its edge signs, and the rooted-forest determinant counts each acyclic subset with its full product of component sizes. The polynomial identity allows signed weights; incidence-minor expansion also gives it by dropping one row in each tree component. Eliminating the n diagonal pivots 3,1,1,-1 gives the claimed Schur matrix and prefactor. With s=b+c and e=b-c the scaled determinant H factors as (1+a-2s-d)(3+a+3d)-3e², agreeing with the stated expansion. The counting convolution is diagonal in the unnormalized Walsh convention with these exact eigenvalues, and column multiplicities are multinomial, so its nullity and rank follow. Modulo two all sign choices give the unsigned value (n+1)(n+3)3^{n-1}, odd for even n. On odd n=2k+1 the type (k,0,0,k+1) zeros the first factor, giving the stated lower bound. At weight two the same-column, same-shore distinct-column, and opposite-shore distinct-column values of H are (n-1)(n+5), n²-4n-17, and (n-5)(n+1), respectively. Weight one gives n²-7 and weight zero is positive. Thus only the opposite-shore distinct-column case at n=5 is singular among these degrees, with exactly 20 such frequencies.
residual_risks: The independent integer edge-subset/Walsh replay agrees for all 1,364 coefficients at n=1 through 5. Type summation reproduces 0,3,0,30,0,245,0,1638 at n=2 through 9, and bounded type and low-weight sweeps support the symbolic result. n=1 is only diagnostic; finite tests do not prove the all-n conclusions. No formal or expert verification is claimed.
